blindSummary: Reconstituted in 2019 as a union territory without its own legislature, so trans-related policy depends on the central government rather than local institutions (a public-records survey places this unit among the 19 with no constitutionally mandated transgender welfare body). Beyond this administrative framework, the country dossier found no region-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern.

A public broadcaster's report (26 March 2026) on the amendment bill narrowing trans self-identification, passed by both houses and pending presidential assent: it limits recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, makes board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery, and sparked protests; the top-court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and critics (including prominent trans and intersex activists) warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people.

A national newspaper (18 August 2024): a transwoman travelling to a medical-college protest alleges a railway-police constable groped her at a metro station as a 'gender check'; police denied it and filed a counter-complaint. Shared national source: it evidences the policing practice of treating trans appearance as a suspicion category, which recurs in checkpoints and transit spaces countrywide rather than in this unit specifically.
